issues.legal_issue: A court cannot prevent residential construction by relying on an earlier open-space designation when an unchallenged approved development plan designates the land for residential use.
material_facts: The land had earlier been earmarked as open space adjoining a school.
An approved development plan later designated the land as residential, and the land was allotted and used as a residential plot.
The public-interest writ petitioner did not challenge the approved plan or its change in land use.
The High Court nevertheless treated the earlier open-space designation as preventing construction.
issues.conclusion: The appeals were allowed, the High Court judgment was set aside, and the writ petition was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 19(1) of the Madhya Pradesh Nagar Tatha Gram Nivesh Adhiniyam, 1973, the approved development plan showing the land as residential became final because it was not challenged. The High Court could not ignore that plan and rely on an earlier open-space designation to prevent construction; no earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: public_interest_writ_challenging_construction and approved_plan_designates_residential and earlier_open_space_designation_changed and plan_change_unchallenged

predicates.public_interest_writ_challenging_constru: A person brought a public-interest writ petition seeking to prevent construction on the land.
predicates.approved_plan_designates_residential: An approved development plan designated the land for residential use.
predicates.earlier_open_space_designation_changed: The land had previously been designated as open space, but that designation was changed to residential use in the approved plan.
predicates.plan_change_unchallenged: The petitioner did not challenge the approved plan or its change in land use.

issues.definition: When a public-interest writ challenges construction, an approved plan designates the land for residential use, an earlier open-space designation was changed, and the plan change is unchallenged, the writ petition is dismissed.
